title: Percentage-of-amount fee at disbursement landing on an exact HALF minor-unit tie: 1% of 1,162,502.50 = 11,625.025, HALF_UP to 11,625.03 (HALF_EVEN would leave 11,625.02).
_note: A NON-ZERO percentage-of-amount fee (calculation_type 2 PERCENT_OF_AMOUNT, charge_time_enum 1 DISBURSEMENT) whose exact product base x rate / 100 lands on exactly one half minor unit: amountPercentageAppliedTo 1162502.500000 x 1.000000% = 11625.025, whose 2-decimal rounding is a tie. The oracle's loan-charge row answers amount 11625.030000 (fee_minor 1162503), i.e. HALF_UP away from zero. Exact integer arithmetic confirms the tie: base 116250250 minor x percentage 1000000 micro-per-cent over percentScale 1e8 leaves quotient 1162502 and remainder exactly half the divisor; HALF_UP rounds that EVEN quotient up by one, while the half-even substitute (charges-wrong-rounding-half-even) would leave 1162502. This is the first stored vector whose fee money cell can see a rounding-mode substitution; FC-09's captured product carries the fraction .55525 and every other stored product is exact, so HALF_UP and HALF_EVEN agree on all of them.

provenance.note: TRANSCRIBED, never computed, from the GET /loans/9/charges observation OHCAPj-loan9-pctamount-disbursement-fee-tie-raw.json under tenant gerege. fee_minor 1162503 is the exact major->minor scaling of the observed amount 11625.030000 (amountPaid 11625.030000, amountOutstanding 0); base_amount_minor 116250250 is the exact major->minor scaling of the observed amountPercentageAppliedTo 1162502.500000; percentage 1000000 is the observed percentage 1.000000 in micro-per-cent. The discriminating cell is the observed HALF_UP answer on the exact .5 tie: HALF_EVEN would transcribe the same bytes as 1162502, so this observation is the one place the two modes differ.
